description:
RuneScape: Dragonwilds update 1.0.1 is here, bringing major combat changes, new ranged weapon special attacks, the Jump Attack, and plenty of quality-of-life improvements! Shortbows can unleash Rapid Fire, Longbows get a powerful Power Shot, and Crossbows gain the Heavy Bolt special attack. You can also recover arrows, slow enemies with leg shots, and dive onto enemies from above.

This update also expands inventory space from 32 to 40 slots, adds dedicated Ring and Amulet slots, introduces the Ultra Compost Bin and Large Compost Bucket, improves item sorting, and addresses save issues and other bugs. Here’s everything worth knowing about the latest RuneScape Dragonwilds patch!

transcript.text: Runescape Dragon Waltz has just dropped its first big update since full release and this is everything you need to know
about it. First up, let's talk about the combat changes. They've added a new jump
attack which can be unlocked through the skill tree and it's called death from above. It allows you to do a sort of
slam attack whenever you're above the maximum height that the double jump arc creates. This means that you can do
things like jump off cliffs or jump off higher ledges and then slam back down doing bonus damage. And yes, you can do
this with wind step too. However, the biggest and probably most requested change in the combat section has to be
the changes to the range skill. They've added a few new things such as ammo recovery and its greater version called
greater ammo recovery into the range skill tree. When you do unlock these, you'll get a chance to recover arrows
from the bodies of anybody that you take down saving you some of your precious ammo. Overall, the range weapon subclass
did receive some other pretty impactful changes though such as all three different bow types now having a special
attack. Short bows have rapid fire which makes you hop backward and fire off three arrows in quick succession. The
longbow is getting power shot which makes you take a knee and draw an arrow for full strength then let it fly
staggering enemies with an enormously powerful shot that has kind of like a sniper since it has crazy amounts of
distance. And the final new special skill comes to the crossbows and it's called heavy bolt. This allows you to
fire a bolt at short distances for a massive increase in damage and it guarantees to apply the enchanted effect
of whatever crossbow bolts you're currently using. It still doesn't stop there for range however as there's one
final change and that is the new low blow skill perk which applies hamstring to your enemies anytime you hit them
below a third of their maximum model height or on their legs so that you can slow them down, making it easier for you
to take them out. It's important to note, however, that this does not work on extremely small mobs or on colossal
enemies, as they are immune to this. Outside of the range skills though, that's not where it ends, as they've
also increased our inventory space from 32 to 40 slots. Now, this doesn't solve the problem of weight, you'll still have
to be worried about it, but you'll no longer have to be as concerned about having one or two of, say, a berry or a
potato sitting in your inventory that you don't care about and end up throwing it away when you could have held onto it
and brought it back to use later. They've also done some changes to mobs here, as they've made it so the aggro
range of enemies is a little bit further, making it less likely for you to have a huge train of enemies
following you around unless that's an intended thing to be happening at that point time. They've also reduced enemy
mob respawn timer, so that when you clear out an area of the world, you're not going to have to worry about coming
back in a day or two and then having all of those mobs there immediately after. When it comes to quality of life
improvements though, they've added some new sort options for your inventory. You can sort by weight, type, or the latest
and most received items, making a little bit easier for you to get what you need when you need it. Arguably the biggest
change is up next though, and that is that they've added a dedicated ring and amulet slot. This means that you can now
have two separate items equipped, one ring and one amulet, just like you can in the original RuneScape games.
Finally, they rounded things off by adding the large compost bucket, which allows you to pour way more compost
instead of having to run around with five or six little ones in order to keep all your farm plots going. In tandem
with that, they've also given you the ultra compost bin, since super just kind of wasn't cutting it anymore for some of
these higher tier farms that people are building. To round everything out though, here are some quick minor
changes that are still fairly impactful and you should know about. First off, they've made it so Overdrive can now
actually be used on the advanced spinning wheel, so that's a nice little plus. Rune arrows and bolts are also now
doing more damage than adamantite as they should have in the first place. The fishing cape now correctly will display
its skill cape perk, which it did not do before. And in case you didn't know, we actually just found this out ourselves,
that it gives you a small chance to instantly catch a fish. And finally, they've made it so that when you're
doing the Scorched Wilderness rate endgame and you reset it for your next run-through, all the enemies and
obstacles will now respawn instead of staying dead from your last run. But let me know what you guys think about this
patch in the comments. Personally, I think it's a huge plus and a nice addition to the game, but I'm still more
so waiting for the prayer update coming sometime later this year, which we will be making a video on in case you're
interested. If you want to learn more about Dragon Wilds, consider checking out this video.
